title: Fixed restriction and cartesian comparison constructions
statement: Construct the open-site overlap comparison, the comparison between cartesian pullbacks across a commuting square, and the restriction comparison beta. The cartesian comparison first cancels the inverse-site equivalence by its counit, then uses the fixed derived pullback composition along the two equal scheme composites. Its component formula is the mapped counit followed by derived transport. The exact-restriction and site overlap comparisons are obtained from their canonical module-level isomorphisms by derived localization.

source.place: Compatibility of derived pullback and open restriction; composition as in Tag 0D5S.

proof.text: Construct the open-site overlap comparison, the comparison between cartesian pullbacks across a commuting square, and the restriction comparison beta. The cartesian comparison first cancels the inverse-site equivalence by its counit, then uses the fixed derived pullback composition along the two equal scheme composites. Its component formula is the mapped counit followed by derived transport. The exact-restriction and site overlap comparisons are obtained from their canonical module-level isomorphisms by derived localization.

The existing open-square component API is relocated unchanged from PerfectOverlapOpenSquareCube into the comparison module, so the constructor and downstream cube can share it without a cycle. Expand the named open-pullback comparison and pinned square to identify inverse components, take inverses for forward components, then substitute those equalities into the two existing beta component formulas.
